mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% (a historically high level for the post-2008 period) indicates a restrictive monetary policy that reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:2013 Fed funds rate was near 0%, but given value is 4.33 (anomaly for context)
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals a deteriorating labor market, which is associated with negative equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows unemployment above 5.0% in 2009 was associated with negative 5-day returns
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0% over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (by more than 0.3 percentage points) and fall in employment level (by more than 100,000 persons) in the same month indicates a severe labor market contraction, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month AND PAYEMS falls > 100000 in 1 month
evidence_refs: fact:In 2008-2009, similar conditions were observed during the financial crisis
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month AND PAYEMS falls > 100000 in 1 month over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the monetary tightening regime defined by CPIAUCSL > 320 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, the market experiences negative returns due to expectations of further rate hikes and reduced liquidity.
evidence_refs: fact:2013 CPI was at 320.58, FEDFUNDS at 4.33
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 320 AND FEDFUNDS > 4.0% over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A GDP level above 23500 billion (the current level) indicates a strong economy, which is associated with positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:GDP level at 23528.047 in 2013 was above the 2012 average of 23000
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 > 23500 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An industrial production index above 100 (the 2017 base year) indicates a robust manufacturing sector, which is associated with positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO is set to 100 in 2017, so values above 100 indicate growth
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO > 100 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level above 1300 thousand units indicates a strong housing market, which is associated with positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows housing starts above 1300 in 2013 were associated with positive equity returns
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST > 1300 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (falling below 4.0% and remaining below for 3 months) indicates an easing monetary policy, which is associated with positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:In 2013, the Fed funds rate was near 0%, so a decline to below 4.0% would be significant easing
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 4.0% and falling for 3 months over any 2-year rolling window.
